_meta.hard_rule: A fix is 'fixed' ONLY when its full business-chain spec passes end-to-end - never an isolated probe. (B1, 2026-06-09, was falsely declared fixed off a single-insert probe; only the full return->credit->statement->unapply chain exposed the stacked breaks.)
_meta.pass_signal: Every chain is a single DO block that ALWAYS terminates with RAISE EXCEPTION 'SMOKE_PASS_ROLLBACK'. That exact error text = PASS (and guarantees rollback). ANY other error = FAIL.
_meta.spec_contract: Keys are the primary RPC under test. 'covers' lists every RPC the chain exercises - run-smoke.mjs --spec <rpc> matches keys AND covers entries, so one chain can certify several RPCs. Every migration that touches an RPC must have or extend a spec covering it.
_meta.area_tags: Every spec carries an "area" array (business-area tags: billing, inventory, lifecycle, pricing, security, idempotency, regression). run-smoke.mjs --area <area> selects by tag; scripts/run-area.mjs bundles these with the matching vitest slice and DB invariant sweeps.

create_order_from_blend_ticket.description: CONTAINER ONLY - run via scripts/smoke/prove-blend-ticket-fractional-cents.mjs, never through run-smoke.mjs against the live database: the chain INSERTs a customer, blend ticket and order, which the LIVE-DATA GUARD correctly refuses. CRX-MONEY-001 (fixed live by 20260811200000, ledger 20260811220045): create_order_from_blend_ticket finished by overwriting the orders header from raw unrounded price x converted-quantity sums, so any blend ticket whose quantity produced a sub-cent line value violated orders_total_cost_whole_cents_chk / orders_total_profit_whole_cents_chk and rolled back the entire completed-ticket-to-order transaction. Latent, never hit in production - no blend ticket has ever produced an order. The prover reads the PRE-FIX body from 20260714230200 and the POST-FIX body from 20260811200000, refusing to run unless the post-fix md5 still equals a pinned snapshot of production pg_proc taken 2026-08-11 - a historical reading, not a live one, since the container has no network, so it catches the repo drifting off what was applied rather than production changing underneath. Six stages: A the pre-fix body violates the whole-cent CHECK; B the migration applies verbatim and its own $ postcondition passes; C the fixed body books whole-cent totals equal to the canonical sum-of-rounded-lines, reports back what it stored, links the ticket, replays idempotently and keeps SECURITY DEFINER, a pinned search_path and no anon/PUBLIC EXECUTE; D re-applying with after_order_items_change dropped FAILS CLOSED; E re-applying with that trigger set REPLICA-only also FAILS CLOSED, which the widespread tgenabled <> 'D' idiom would not catch; F characterizes the one residual gap - the trigger guarantee is APPLY-time only, so with the fixed body and the trigger dropped at RUN time the RPC reports success and books a zero-value header. Ends in SMOKE_PASS_ROLLBACK at stage C. Every helper body in the fixture is md5-verified against live pg_proc EXCEPT link_blend_ticket_to_order, which is a deliberate behavior-equivalent stand-in (live is 8.3 KB across tables the fixture trims) - it is therefore NOT listed in covers; real coverage for it lives in the create_blend_ticket chain.

The candidate renames the live body to _create_inventory_hold_intent_impl_20260905 (postgres-only EXECUTE) and installs a same-signature wrapper that requires the key, gates on an ACTIVE admin/sales_rep profile NULL-safely, fingerprints the request, calls check_idempotency_intent (per-key advisory lock) before any mutation, then binds the receipt. The chain proves: one keyed hold creates one row and one bound receipt; an identical retry (5 vs 5.0) replays the same hold_id and inserts nothing; a changed quantity, notes or expiry on the retained key is REFUSED with IDEMPOTENCY_INTENT_MISMATCH whose DETAIL carries the committed hold, and inserts nothing; a second actor reusing the key gets IDEMPOTENCY_ACTOR_MISMATCH; NULL and blank keys are refused with IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED before any work; a caller with NO profile row and a deactivated admin both get INSUFFICIENT_ROLE (the live body's v_role NOT IN let a missing profile through); unauthenticated gets AUTH_REQUIRED and a forged p_performed_by gets ACTOR_MISMATCH; a pre-migration receipt carrying neither binding column fails closed; cross-operation key reuse still raises; INSUFFICIENT_HOLD_INVENTORY and FORCE_REQUIRES_ADMIN are unchanged and leave neither a hold nor a receipt; an admin force with a reason still works, is receipted and replays identically; a NULL p_force replays the false-force receipt as the identical request; and the impl is not executable by anon, authenticated or service_role. The prover replays the 2026-07-27 baseline plus every later migration in a network-isolated Supabase PostgreSQL 17 container, asserts the baseline body hash matches the candidate's pin, proves the chain FAILS and a two-session same-key race against the live body leaves ONE hold with the loser ERRORING (IDEMPOTENCY_CONCURRENT_REPLAY_RETRY), applies the candidate, then proves the chain passes, the same race leaves ONE hold with BOTH sessions succeeding and returning the same hold_id and a receipt bound to the actor, and the candidate re-applies cleanly. Ends in SMOKE_PASS_ROLLBACK.
